newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CHEMICAL LOBBY SEES '96 OUTPUT UP 1 TO 2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CHEMICAL LOBBY SEES '96 OUTPUT UP 1 TO 2 PCT.

text.p: The Finnish chemical industry lobby said on Wednesday it expects its 1996 production to increase one to two percent on 1995.
"Due to low starting level, production will not increase more than one to two percent on last year," the Chemical Industry Federation of Finland said.
The federation said it expects its 1996 result after financial items to improve clearly on 1995, when it amounted to eight percent of net sales.
The lobby said it expects 1996 net sales of the sector's companies to increase three percent on 1995.
It did not give precise figures nor did it specify whether its growth outlook referred to value or volume.
"On the whole, the chemical industry's prospects are good," the federation said.
But it added that the output of chemicals and chemical products has been clouded by weak demand in the forest industry.
The oil refining industry has suffered from narrow margins but recent data indicated that the situation was improving, the federation said.
There had been a clear growth trend in the production of rubber and plastic products since the beginning of 1996, but the price development had not been as favourable.
